comparator.name: Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The September-2026 programme and adopted TSB Appendix 1d establish the Dutch Sociology track, sixty credits per year and the retained twenty-four-credit Urban Issues major. Its named twelve-credit Year-2 project and twelve-credit thesis are the Urban Issues variants. The non-exchange pathway retains a compulsory twelve-credit placement and eighteen genuinely open credits. The separate twelve-credit restricted choice is instantiated as Global Migration and Sociology of Work, both permitted six-credit subjects from a non-selected major. The major and these choices are selected independently of UCR fit. Non-credit GROW is not added to the degree total. Thesis admission requires the full propaedeutic phase plus sixty postpropaedeutic credits; the Spring thesis follows completion of both earlier years. The placement requires an approved plan and signed contract before starting and at least 336 hours.

components.name: Academische Vaardigheden Sociologie 2
components.note: Academic Skills 2 builds on Skills 1; Skills 3 builds on both and on introductory methods, with statistics alongside. The first-year research project then applies these foundations.

components.name: Sociological Research Project 2: Urban Issues
components.note: This is the twelve-credit Urban Issues research-project variant. It applies earlier quantitative and qualitative methods to a complete group sociological investigation, report and presentation.

components.name: Stage
components.note: The non-exchange pathway requires a placement of at least 336 hours in a relevant organisation. An approved learning plan and signed contract are required before starting. Supervision and a reflective final report complete the assessment; no host is assumed.

components.name: Open elective space
components.note: Eighteen credits remain genuinely open for a minor, free electives or a permitted combination, including approved study abroad. No particular minor or course package is imposed.

components.name: Global Migration
components.note: Selected as one of two six-credit restricted choices from non-selected majors. Global Migration examines migration theories, labour and refugee flows, and relations with sending and receiving societies.

components.name: Sociology of Work
components.note: Selected as the second permitted six-credit restricted choice. Sociology of Work examines work, class, power, gender and race, including technological and ecological changes.

components.name: Thesis Urban Issues
components.note: The twelve-credit Urban Issues thesis is an individual empirical study with a research proposal, article-style paper, peer feedback and symposium presentation. Entry requires completion of all first-year courses and at least 60 postpropaedeutic EC. Both earlier years are completed before the normal Spring thesis; an Autumn thesis is exceptional.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is Tilburg’s Dutch Sociology bachelor, which focuses on Dutch society. Of the three published majors, Grootstedelijke Vraagstukken is the Dutch-taught route and directly continues the programme’s stated attention to Dutch cities, inequality, exclusion and the welfare state. alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme uses the complete available UCR sociology sequence and a strong mixed-method social-research spine. The culture/identity/migration and social-risks/health/sustainability directions are independently supported by generator-eligible programme interests and the official curriculum, produce substantively different course choices, and pass feasibility and pairwise distinctness. Production therefore stops at the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop literature evaluation, academic argument, research questions and scholarly writing. UCR combines these with personal development and civic collaboration; Tilburg specifically develops sections of sociological research articles.

Both examine welfare-state institutions and distributional choices affecting inequality and exclusion. UCR uses public-economic models and policy evaluation rather than a dedicated sociological exclusion perspective.
Both develop empirical design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling and introductory analysis. UCR additionally includes a substantial team data-collection project.

Both concern questionnaire measurement and quantitative analysis. UCR designs and pilots a psychological survey and evaluates reliability and associations; Tilburg provides the dedicated questionnaire construction/analysis course with an SPSS assessment.

Both develop data retrieval, preparation, recoding, analysis, visual/tabular presentation and interpretation. UCR has broader tabular, spatial and text-data workflows; Tilburg explicitly connects these skills to sociological questions.

Both develop normative reflection on responsibility and justice. UCR supplies ethical theories and practical moral argument; Tilburg specifically examines power, group agency, social responsibility and epistemic injustice.
Both examine political institutions, actors and behaviour through political-science concepts and comparative analysis.
Both introduce sociological questions, concepts, classical theories and relations among individuals, institutions and societies.
Both develop qualitative design, interviewing, coding, thematic interpretation, ethics and research reporting.
Both develop contemporary sociological theory and use it to interpret society; UCR also emphasises colonial and postcolonial criticism.

Both substantively examine inequality and collective responses. UCR focuses on environmental injustice and movements; Tilburg specifically deepens educational and labour inequalities, including intergenerational transmission and school-to-work transitions.

Both analyse how public spheres and institutions define, contest and respond to social problems. UCR focuses on civil society, trust, solidarity and social repair; Tilburg explicitly studies competing problem owners, historical framing, media and the distinction between social, sociological and policy problems.

Both examine health, social determinants and implications for policy. UCR develops epidemiological designs, causal interpretation and public-health assessment; Tilburg specifically studies how individual and social circumstances shape health across the life course.
Both examine social cognition, attitudes, influence, groups and interpersonal behaviour using empirical psychological evidence.

Both develop ANOVA, correlation, multivariable regression and logistic analysis with software, model choice and interpretation. UCR applies these to behavioural/health evidence; Tilburg integrates them into the sociological methods sequence.

Scholarly reading and source evaluation occur in selected courses, but their strongest placements are with research writing and data skills; none is counted again as the first dedicated skills module.
Introductory statistical work is present in Research Methods/Statistics and advanced analysis. Their strongest placements are with methods and causal techniques; no course is counted twice.
The selected courses provide related theory or methods elsewhere, but no additional course is counted as this dedicated sociological component.

Selected courses include original empirical projects, but their primary placements represent methods, qualitative inquiry and survey analysis. No second course is counted as this separate sociological research-project requirement.
Research and ethical reflection contribute elsewhere, but no selected course provides a dedicated social-science philosophy/epistemology course.
The dedicated twelve-credit Urban Issues group research project is not replaced by generic research work already represented elsewhere.
Policy, inequality, race, gender and public-health study support urban questions, but no selected course centres urban sociology and metropolitan neighbourhood dynamics.
A compulsory 336-hour sociological placement is not a scheduled UCR course; no host or internship is invented.
Eighteen open credits remain unspecified; no minor or elective package is invented.
Rights and transnational institutions contribute to migration questions, but no selected course centres the sociology of migration flows and sending/receiving societies.
The leadership survey has its strongest placement with questionnaire methods. No additional course centres the dedicated sociological history and theory of work.
The individual twelve-credit Urban Issues empirical thesis remains a required Tilburg component. Optional UCR independent research is separate from scheduled credits.

blocks.title: Other dedicated Sociology requirements and open choice

comparator.note: This is the twelve-credit Urban Issues research-project variant. It applies earlier quantitative and qualitative methods to a complete group sociological investigation, report and presentation.

The non-exchange pathway requires a placement of at least 336 hours in a relevant organisation. An approved learning plan and signed contract are required before starting. Supervision and a reflective final report complete the assessment; no host is assumed.
Eighteen credits remain genuinely open for a minor, free electives or a permitted combination, including approved study abroad. No particular minor or course package is imposed.

Selected as one of two six-credit restricted choices from non-selected majors. Global Migration examines migration theories, labour and refugee flows, and relations with sending and receiving societies.
Selected as the second permitted six-credit restricted choice. Sociology of Work examines work, class, power, gender and race, including technological and ecological changes.

The twelve-credit Urban Issues thesis is an individual empirical study with a research proposal, article-style paper, peer feedback and symposium presentation. Entry requires completion of all first-year courses and at least 60 postpropaedeutic EC. Both earlier years are completed before the normal Spring thesis; an Autumn thesis is exceptional.

notes.text: UCR can combine sociological theory and empirical methods with political, cultural, health and environmental perspectives. Tilburg provides a prescribed disciplinary methods sequence, a twenty-four-credit major, a compulsory placement and an individual sociology thesis. The partial relationships shown do not reproduce that full structure.

audience.programmeDescription: Sociology at Tilburg studies social relations, institutions, inequality and change through theory and empirical research. This example follows the Urban Issues major, chooses Global Migration and Sociology of Work as restricted electives, and retains open choice, a sociological placement and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can develop a broad sociology and policy programme, a cultural/identity focus or a social-risk focus. Its courses provide meaningful theory, research and interdisciplinary study, while Tilburg supplies a more prescribed sociology curriculum, an urban major, a required placement and thesis. Relationships shown are partial.
